findings.finding: The 2026-09-18 securities purchase agreement bars the company from issuing ordinary shares or convertible securities from 09-18 until 30 days after the 09-21 closing (to about 2026-10-21). By my derivation from baseline bars, both reset warrant series sit above today's ~$2 spot. So no new primary supply can price tonight, and no fresh cashless-exercise supply is in the money inside the window.
findings.mechanism_in_window: The standstill covers the entire 10-13 close to 10-14 close window. It removes the overnight offering or ATM draw that is the commonest second shoe for a post-reverse-split microcap.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Since the 09-21 closing the stock fell on 10 of 12 >=6% drop days. The supply came from the raise itself, the reverse split and warrant resets, not from a new offering. There is no prior instance of a new offering inside this standstill, because none was permitted.
findings.why_not_priced: The price treats DCX like a generic serial diluter, falling 9% on 46x volume with no news. A dated contractual bar on new issuance through the window is something most of today's fallers with open ATMs do not have. If the market held this, the intraday fade would have been shallower than the name's own continuation pattern, and it was not.
findings.independence: Warrant terms (Series B 30-day expiry from the 2026-09-21 issuance date; reset to the lowest VWAP from 5 trading days before to 5 after the share-combination date, so the window closed about 2026-10-05) are at https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/1957413/000149315226043615/ex4-2.htm and the 6-K of 2026-09-24. The reset price relative to spot is my inference from baseline closes (Oct-5 close about $3.38 derived), not a published number.
